title: Genetic Analysis of Platelet-Related Genes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
author: Li, Zhao, et al.
materials: With the purpose of down-regulating the expression of PRKCD in HCC cells, siRNAs were selected for targeted gene silencing and their primer sequences were listed below: negative control siRNA (si-NC): sense: 5′-UUCUCCGAACGUGUCACGUTT-3′, anti-sense: 5′-ACGUGACACGUUCGGAGAATT-3′; si-PRKCD-1: sense: 5′-CCAUGGUGAUGAUGAGGAUTT-3′, anti-sense: 5′-AUCCUCAUCAUCACCAUGGTT-3′; si-PRKCD-2: sense: 5′-GCAGCAAGUGCAACAUCAATT-3′, anti-sense: 5′-UUGAUGUUGCACUUGCUGCTT-3′), which were synthesized and obtained from the DesignGene Biotechnology (Shanghai, China). HCC cells in well condition were uniformly seeded into 6-well plates in advance, and transfection was performed with Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen, CA, USA) following the manufacturer’s instruction when the cells were adherent and reached 70% confluence.

Both OS and PFS time demonstrated that there was an obvious survival discrepancy between the two HCC subtypes, a poorer prognosis was observed in patients belonging to cluster C2 compared with those in cluster C1 (Fig. 4B). Whereafter, the intrinsic connection between HCC clusters and clinicopathological parameters was analyzed, and Fig. 4C displayed that cases in cluster C2 were closely associated with the higher expression of most PRGs and worse clinical features including T stage, tumor stage, and pathological grade, which also confirmed the poor prognosis of this HCC subtype. To further explore the discrepancies in functional pathways and immune features between different clusters, we performed GSVA and ssGSEA analyses in R software. As Fig. 4D displayed, compared to cluster C1, the C2 subtype mainly enriched in KEGG pathways like Cell cycle, Homologous recombination, DNA replication, cancer-associated (like Bladder, Pancreatic, and Renal cell carcinomas) pathways, and signaling transduction axis including NOD-like receptor and mTOR signaling pathways, implying that cluster C2 might own a close association with the occurrence and evolution of HCC. steps.title: Prepare siRNA reagents
steps.instruction: Obtain the following siRNAs (synthesized by DesignGene Biotechnology, Shanghai, China): negative control siRNA (si‑NC) sense 5′‑UUCUCCGAACGUGUCACGUTT‑3′ / antisense 5′‑ACGUGACACGUUCGGAGAATT‑3′; si‑PRKCD‑1 sense 5′‑CCAUGGUGAUGAUGAGGAUTT‑3′ / antisense 5′‑AUCCUCAUCAUCACCAUGGTT‑3′; si‑PRKCD‑2 sense 5′‑GCAGCAAGUGCAACAUCAATT‑3′ / antisense 5′‑UUGAUGUUGCACUUGCUGCTT‑3′. Aliquot and store according to the supplier’s instructions.

steps.title: Transfect HCC cells with siRNA
steps.instruction: Seed HCC cells in 6‑well plates and culture until they reach ~70 % confluence. Prepare transfection complexes using Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen, CA, USA) following the manufacturer’s protocol, adding the appropriate siRNA (negative control or PRKCD‑targeting). Add the complexes to the cells, incubate under standard culture conditions, and allow gene silencing to proceed as per experimental design.

steps.title: Platelet‑cell co‑culture for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Seed the transfected HCC cells (negative control and PRKCD‑silenced) into a 24‑well plate at ~80 % confluence. After cells have adhered, add isolated platelets directly to each well and incubate for 30 min at 37 °C. Harvest the cell‑platelet mixtures for flow cytometric analysis.

substeps.instruction: Stain the harvested cells with the following antibodies: FITC‑anti‑human CD61 (catalog 336,404; Biolegend, USA), PE‑anti‑human CD62P (catalog 304,906; Biolegend, USA), and Alexa Fluor® 647‑anti‑human CD41/CD61 (catalog 362,806; Biolegend, USA).
Acquire data on a Beckman Coulter CytoFlex flow cytometer.
Analyze platelet activation (CD62P, CD41/CD61) using FlowJo software.
Repeat the entire experiment independently at least three times.
